story_type: sailboat sinking far offshore, ship rescues raft
hook: Three men in their 70s, 1,200 miles from Cape Cod, sinking.
narration: Three sailors in their seventies, twelve hundred miles off Cape Cod, and their boat was taking on water.
The seas were running ten to twelve feet, with thirty-three knot winds.
A Coast Guard Hercules crew found them and dropped flares, a life raft and a radio.
The men abandoned their boat and climbed into the raft.
This far out, no helicopter can reach you, so the Coast Guard asks any ship in the area to turn around and help.
The crew of a fishing boat, the Robero, diverted through those seas to reach the raft. [short pause]
outcome: The Robero rescued all three sailors, still wearing their life jackets.
title: Sinking 1,200 miles off Cape Cod
description:
Three sailors in their 70s abandoned their sinking sailboat Tao for a life raft about 1,200 miles off Cape Cod, Massachusetts, on May 15, 2014, and were rescued by the fishing vessel Robero after a Coast Guard request.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Coast Guard Air Station Elizabeth City, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/337196/coast-guard-rescues-sailors-1200-miles-southeast-cape-cod

extra_sources.excerpt: Three Frenchmen in their 70s were rescued Thursday afternoon about 1,200 miles off Cape Cod, Mass., after their boat began to take on water. The Hercules crew arrived at the scene of the emergency about 11 a.m. and dropped marking flares, a life raft and a radio to the crew, who abandoned their boat and got into the raft. The Robero arrived about 2 p.m. and rescued the sailors, who were reported to be wearing life jackets. Seas were running 10 to 12 feet, with 33-knot winds.
